plant.verbatim: Grey walls and ceiling; it looked better a few versions ago.

seat.BEST_WHY: The lit floor between the figure and the bottom of the frame (roughly x 300–620, y 460–640) is genuinely constructed, not stamped. Slab widths vary along a single course — the slab left of the figure runs about three grid units wide, the two to its right are one and two — and the joints between them are drawn at different depths, some a single dark pixel, some a two-pixel trench with a lighter chipped lip on the upper side. The diagonal chisel hatching stays *inside* individual slabs and stops at the joints, which is what tells you the stone was cut and dressed one piece at a time rather than having a texture laid over the top. The lighting is also physically honest: the patch at x 285–360, y 450–545 measures mean luminance 109.7 and its mirror on the other side of the figure at x 465–540 measures 100.6 — near-symmetric around a point light, as it should be. The block course running along the bottom edge of the middle wall at y ≈ 420–428 is the best-made thing in the deck: irregular block lengths, dark joints of varying weight, and one block near x 545 that is visibly lighter than its neighbours, so the run reads as repaired rather than built.
seat.WORST_WHY: The green water body at the right is a rectangle. Its left edge is a dead-straight vertical at x ≈ 248 running the full height of the pool, and its bottom is a dead-straight horizontal at y ≈ 190, and where the brown dirt meets it there is no bank, no wet margin, no edge tile, no darkening — the dirt simply stops on a pixel boundary and water begins. Water does not have corners. Beneath that: the frame is lit uniformly from nowhere, with zero falloff anywhere in it. The two barrels at x 110–145 and x 155–190, y 190–215, are the identical sprite placed twice with the identical lid highlight in the identical position. The dirt field repeats a single 16px tile with a recognisable dark-red speckle cluster that recurs on a visible grid across the whole middle of the frame. The bottom stone band is one flagstone tile with every joint identical on every instance. The projection is inconsistent within one image: the barrels and the crates at x 62–96 are drawn in three-quarter view showing their sides and lids, while the floor is straight top-down, and the wall band at the bottom is drawn as a flat front elevation. And the white pixel scatter at x 208–232, y 110–125 has no silhouette at all — it is a handful of loose white and grey pixels that reads as dirt on the screen rather than as an object.
seat.FLAGGED:
2, 3

For 3, the flag is a lighting fault you see instantly: the pale wedge on the floor to the *left* of the figure, x 285–360, y 450–545, measures mean luminance 123.8, while the mirror patch at the same distance on the *right*, x 465–540, measures 68.8. Eighteen-tenths as bright on one side of a point light with nothing occluding the other side. There is no wall, pillar or step between the lamp and the right-hand patch that is not also on the left. It looks like a highlight was painted in by hand and the other side forgotten.

For 2, the flag is the rectangular water plus the duplicated barrels — either one alone is a glance-level tell.
